title: SailPoint Engineer Domain 9 questions (9.1)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with SailPoint.

questions.stem: A network team asks how VAs talk to the SailPoint tenant. Which description is correct?
choices: The tenant opens inbound SSH connections to each VA host on port 22
The VA and tenant exchange files over plain FTP
The VA opens outbound TLS connections on port 443 to the tenant
The tenant reaches the VA through a site-to-site VPN it initiates
questions.answer: The VA opens outbound TLS connections on port 443 to the tenant
questions.explanation: VAs initiate outbound HTTPS to SailPoint, so no inbound internet connections to the VA are needed. SSH on port 22 is for local admin access only.

questions.stem: Which protocol protects traffic between an admin's browser or API client and the ISC tenant?
choices: TLS 1.2 or higher over HTTPS
IPsec tunnels from each admin site
SSH with key-based sign-in
Plain HTTP with an IP allow list
questions.answer: TLS 1.2 or higher over HTTPS
questions.explanation: Access to the tenant UI and APIs is over HTTPS with modern TLS. An IP allow list is not encryption.

questions.stem: An auditor asks whether AD data is encrypted all the way from the domain controllers to the tenant. The AD source uses plain LDAP. What is the BEST answer?
choices: All hops are encrypted because the VA tunnels all of its traffic
The VA-to-cloud hop uses TLS; the VA-to-DC hop needs LDAPS
No hop is encrypted until the data is finally stored at rest in the tenant
Only the hop from the DC to the VA is encrypted
questions.answer: The VA-to-cloud hop uses TLS; the VA-to-DC hop needs LDAPS
questions.explanation: The VA-to-tenant link is always TLS, but the hop to the target follows the source's own settings. Turning on SSL for the source closes the gap.

questions.stem: Security requires encrypted traffic between the VAs and a SQL Server used by a JDBC source. Where is this BEST configured?
choices: In the identity profile that uses the source
In the VA cluster's time zone settings
In the tenant's password and session policy
In the JDBC connection URL's encryption properties
questions.answer: In the JDBC connection URL's encryption properties
questions.explanation: Driver-level encryption, such as encrypt=true for SQL Server, is set in the connection URL or driver properties. Identity profiles and password policies do not affect the database link.

questions.stem: A firewall team wants to know which side starts connections between the corporate network and the SailPoint cloud. What should the engineer tell them?
choices: The cloud starts all connections into the VAs
The VAs start all connections outbound; the cloud never connects in
Each side starts the connections it needs for its own scheduled jobs
Connections start from the domain controllers directly into the cloud
questions.answer: The VAs start all connections outbound; the cloud never connects in
questions.explanation: Because VAs initiate outbound connections, no inbound ports from the internet are opened. Domain controllers never talk to the cloud directly.

questions.stem: The AD connector uses IQService on a Windows server for mailbox creation. Security requires that link to be encrypted. What does the design need?
choices: IQService installed on the VA itself
IQService reached through the SailPoint cloud instead of the VA
IQService protected only by an IP allow list
IQService set up for TLS with a certificate the VAs trust
questions.answer: IQService set up for TLS with a certificate the VAs trust
questions.explanation: IQService supports TLS, and the VAs must trust its certificate to connect. Allow lists limit who connects but do not encrypt.

questions.stem: A security reviewer worries that new passwords typed into ISC could be read by SailPoint in transit to the target. What design feature addresses this?
choices: The tenant stores the password in clear text for one hour, then deletes it
The VA emails the password to the target owner
The browser encrypts it with the VA's public key before sending
The browser sends the password over plain HTTP straight to the VA host
questions.answer: The browser encrypts it with the VA's public key before sending
questions.explanation: With zero knowledge encryption, the password is encrypted in the browser with the VA's 2048-bit RSA public key so only the VA can decrypt it. SailPoint's cloud cannot read it.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes how ISC protects tenant data at rest?
choices: It is encrypted with strong encryption such as AES-256
It is stored in clear text inside a private, firewalled network
It is encrypted only when a customer opts in
It is protected only by user levels
questions.answer: It is encrypted with strong encryption such as AES-256
questions.explanation: SailPoint encrypts tenant data at rest with strong encryption such as AES-256 by default. User levels control access but do not encrypt.

questions.stem: A report admin downloads a CSV report of identities to a laptop. Who is responsible for protecting that copy?
choices: SailPoint, because the report was generated inside the tenant
The customer, because it now sits outside SailPoint's cloud
The VA, because it encrypts all exports
The source owner, because the data first came from their application
questions.answer: The customer, because it now sits outside SailPoint's cloud
questions.explanation: Once data leaves the tenant, the customer must protect it under its own policies. SailPoint's encryption at rest covers data in the cloud service.

questions.stem: A VA's logs can include account names and error details. What is the BEST way to protect this data on premises?
choices: Copy the logs to a public file share for review
Disable logging on every VA
Store copies of the VA disk images on removable media at another site
Restrict console and SSH access to the VAs and their hypervisor
questions.answer: Restrict console and SSH access to the VAs and their hypervisor
questions.explanation: VA logs live on customer infrastructure, so access to the VMs and host must be limited. Turning off logging removes the tool needed for troubleshooting.

questions.stem: An auditor asks whether tenant backups are protected the same way as live data. What is the BEST answer?
choices: No, backups are kept in clear text so that restores run faster
No, customers must encrypt SailPoint's backups with their own keys
Yes, backups are encrypted at rest like live tenant data
Yes, but only for flat file sources
questions.answer: Yes, backups are encrypted at rest like live tenant data
questions.explanation: SailPoint's encryption at rest covers stored copies, including backups. Customers do not manage SailPoint's internal backups.

questions.stem: A delimited file with HR data is uploaded to a source. How is that data protected once it is in the tenant?
choices: It is stored encrypted at rest like other tenant data
It stays on the admin's laptop and is read on demand
It is stored unencrypted because files are not records
It is held only on the VA that parsed it
questions.answer: It is stored encrypted at rest like other tenant data
questions.explanation: Uploaded data becomes tenant data and is encrypted at rest. Delimited file data does not pass through or stay on a VA.

questions.stem: Under the shared responsibility model, which task belongs to the customer for data security?
choices: Encrypting the tenant's databases and backups
Managing the cloud's storage keys
Patching SailPoint's multi-tenant cloud services
Choosing what data to aggregate and who can see it
questions.answer: Choosing what data to aggregate and who can see it
questions.explanation: SailPoint secures and encrypts the service, while customers decide what data enters it and who can access it through user levels. Storage keys and patching are SailPoint's job.

questions.stem: A team wants to reduce the impact if any copy of identity data were ever exposed. What is the MOST effective step they control?
choices: Collect only the attributes and accounts the program needs
Add more identity attributes now in case they are needed later on
Store national IDs as identity attributes
Aggregate every source as often as possible to keep data fresh
questions.answer: Collect only the attributes and accounts the program needs
questions.explanation: Data minimization limits what could ever be exposed. More attributes or more frequent runs increase exposure.

questions.stem: An admin saves the password for a VA-based source. Who can decrypt it?
choices: Any SailPoint support engineer
Only the VAs in the source's cluster
Any admin with the Source Admin user level
Any VA in any cluster of the tenant
questions.answer: Only the VAs in the source's cluster
questions.explanation: Source credentials are encrypted with the cluster's public key, and only that cluster's VAs hold the private key. Admins can replace credentials but not read them.

questions.stem: A second VA is added to a cluster, and tasks on it fail with decryption errors while the first VA works. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The new VA has more memory than the first
The cluster has a time zone set
The new VA's keyPassphrase differs from the cluster's
The cluster's sources list two domain controllers
questions.answer: The new VA's keyPassphrase differs from the cluster's
questions.explanation: Every VA in a cluster must use the identical keyPassphrase so they share the key. A mismatch means the new VA cannot decrypt the credentials.

questions.stem: Which command sets the keyPassphrase during VA setup for a commercial tenant?
choices: sudo passwd sailpoint
va-bootstrap reset-tenant
va-bootstrap set-passphrase
sudo systemctl set-passphrase ccg
questions.answer: va-bootstrap set-passphrase
questions.explanation: va-bootstrap set-passphrase stores the passphrase in the VA's configuration. passwd only changes the sailpoint user's sign-in password.

questions.stem: Which keyPassphrase meets SailPoint's rules for VA setup?
choices: !Harbor2026Lantern
Harbor 2026 Lantern
Harbor/2026/Lantern
Harbor2026Lantern
questions.answer: Harbor2026Lantern
questions.explanation: The passphrase cannot start with a special character or contain !, /, \ or spaces. The other three break those rules.

questions.stem: An engineer opens config.yaml on a VA and sees the keyPassphrase starting with a run of colons. What does this mean?
choices: The VA has encrypted the passphrase it stores
The passphrase was entered incorrectly
The VA is not yet paired with a cluster
The passphrase has expired and must be reset
questions.answer: The VA has encrypted the passphrase it stores
questions.explanation: The VA encrypts the stored keyPassphrase automatically, and encrypted values start with ::::. It is normal, not an error.

questions.stem: A source is moved from one VA cluster to another. What should the engineer expect to do?
choices: Nothing, because the same credentials are shared by every cluster in the tenant
Re-enter the credentials so they are encrypted for the new cluster
Copy the old cluster's config.yaml file to every VA in the new cluster
Ask SailPoint support to decrypt and move them
questions.answer: Re-enter the credentials so they are encrypted for the new cluster
questions.explanation: Credentials are encrypted for a specific cluster's key, so the new cluster cannot use the old ciphertext. Copying files or asking SailPoint to decrypt breaks the key design.

questions.stem: Why does SailPoint design source credentials so that only the customer's VAs can decrypt them?
choices: So that admins can read the saved credentials directly in the Admin UI
So a cloud breach does not expose target system passwords
So credentials can be emailed to source owners
So that VAs can share saved credentials with other customers' tenants
questions.answer: So a cloud breach does not expose target system passwords
questions.explanation: Keeping the private key on customer VAs means the cloud stores only ciphertext. Admins cannot read saved credentials in the UI.

questions.stem: What is SailPoint's minimum recommendation for VAs in a production cluster?
choices: Exactly one VA so that tasks are never split
One VA per source in the tenant
At least two VAs so the cluster survives one failure
One VA plus nightly snapshots of its disk
questions.answer: At least two VAs so the cluster survives one failure
questions.explanation: At least two VAs per cluster give high availability; if one stops, the other keeps working. Snapshots restore later but do not keep work running.

questions.stem: One of three VAs in a cluster fails during the day. What happens to work for the cluster's sources?
choices: All sources stop until the failed VA returns
The tenant runs the connectors in the cloud instead
Only authoritative sources keep running
The remaining VAs in the cluster keep processing it
questions.answer: The remaining VAs in the cluster keep processing it
questions.explanation: Any healthy VA in a cluster can take the cluster's tasks. The cloud does not run VA-based connectors itself.

questions.stem: A company has two isolated networks with no routing between them, each holding different applications. How should the VAs be designed?
choices: One cluster per network, each with at least two VAs
One cluster with one VA in each network
One VA in total, with new routes opened to both networks
One cluster hosted in the SailPoint cloud for both networks
questions.answer: One cluster per network, each with at least two VAs
questions.explanation: A cluster's VAs must all reach the cluster's sources, so isolated networks need their own clusters. Mixing them would make tasks fail on the VA that cannot reach the target.

questions.stem: Both data centers can reach the same applications. The company wants work to continue if one data center is lost. What is the BEST design?
choices: Place VAs from both data centers in the same cluster
Place every VA in the primary data center for simpler support
Keep one VA powered off in the secondary site until needed
Rely on the tenant to run the connectors
questions.answer: Place VAs from both data centers in the same cluster
questions.explanation: VAs in both sites within one cluster keep tasks running when one site fails, provided both can reach the sources. A powered-off VA needs manual action.

questions.stem: VAs in a cluster need a reboot to clear cached jobs. How should the engineer do it to keep the cluster available?
choices: Reboot every VA at the same moment
Delete the cluster and create a new one
Power off the VAs until the next maintenance window
Reboot one VA at a time and confirm each is healthy
questions.answer: Reboot one VA at a time and confirm each is healthy
questions.explanation: Rebooting one VA at a time keeps the others serving tasks. Rebooting all at once causes an outage for every source in the cluster.

questions.stem: A cluster has three VAs, but an AD source lists a single domain controller. What is the remaining single point of failure?
choices: The number of VAs configured in the cluster
The tenant's storage in the SailPoint cloud
The one domain controller configured on the source
The keyPassphrase of the cluster
questions.answer: The one domain controller configured on the source
questions.explanation: VA redundancy does not help if the only listed DC is down. Listing several DCs adds source-side redundancy.

questions.stem: Several large sources share one cluster, and aggregations queue behind each other. What is a sound design change?
choices: Remove VAs from the cluster so tasks run in a fixed, predictable order
Add VAs to the cluster so more tasks can run in parallel
Move every large source to delimited file uploads instead
Set every source as authoritative
questions.answer: Add VAs to the cluster so more tasks can run in parallel
questions.explanation: More VAs in a cluster add capacity as well as redundancy. Removing VAs reduces both.

questions.stem: How does SailPoint provide resilience for the ISC cloud service itself?
choices: It runs on a single server in each customer's network
It runs on AWS across multiple availability zones
It relies on customers to host a standby tenant
It runs on the customer's VAs when the cloud fails
questions.answer: It runs on AWS across multiple availability zones
questions.explanation: ISC is a multi-tenant SaaS on AWS using several availability zones. VAs are connectors, not a fallback for the cloud service.

questions.stem: Which redundancy task is the customer's responsibility in an ISC deployment?
choices: Scaling the tenant's microservices under load
Replicating the tenant's databases across zones
Patching SailPoint's cloud servers
Keeping enough healthy VAs and reachable sources
questions.answer: Keeping enough healthy VAs and reachable sources
questions.explanation: SailPoint runs and scales the cloud platform; customers own their VAs, networks and source systems. Database replication is SailPoint's job.

questions.stem: Every VA in a cluster is offline. What still works?
choices: The tenant UI and APIs, but tasks for that cluster's sources wait
Nothing, because the tenant depends on the VAs
All sources, because the cloud runs the connectors itself instead of the VAs
Only aggregations, but not provisioning
questions.answer: The tenant UI and APIs, but tasks for that cluster's sources wait
questions.explanation: The cloud service stays up, but VA-based connector work for that cluster cannot run until a VA reconnects. VAs are not part of the cloud's own redundancy.

questions.stem: Who installs software updates on ISC virtual appliances?
choices: The customer downloads each patch by hand
The source owner updates the VA
SailPoint pushes VA updates automatically
No one, because VAs never change after deployment
questions.answer: SailPoint pushes VA updates automatically
questions.explanation: VAs receive updates from SailPoint automatically; the customer provides the hypervisor, resources and network. Manual patching is not the model.

questions.stem: A bad transform change breaks many identity attributes. Which ISC feature helps restore the earlier configuration?
choices: A Configuration Hub backup taken before the change
A VA snapshot taken before the change
An unoptimized aggregation of every source
A manager certification campaign
questions.answer: A Configuration Hub backup taken before the change
questions.explanation: Configuration Hub backups capture tenant configuration objects so they can be restored. A VA snapshot does not hold tenant configuration.

questions.stem: Why do customers not size or add servers for the ISC cloud service as their identity count grows?
choices: Each tenant has a fixed server that never grows
Customers add capacity by adding more identity profiles
SailPoint scales the multi-tenant services for them
Capacity comes only from adding VAs
questions.answer: SailPoint scales the multi-tenant services for them
questions.explanation: As a SaaS, ISC's cloud services are scaled by SailPoint. VAs add connector capacity, not cloud capacity.

questions.stem: Which TWO design choices BEST improve the availability of VA-based connectivity?
choices: Run at least two VAs in each production cluster
Spread a cluster's VAs across hosts or data centers that reach the sources
Run one VA and take nightly snapshots of it
Give each VA a different keyPassphrase
Turn off automatic VA updates
answers: Run at least two VAs in each production cluster
Spread a cluster's VAs across hosts or data centers that reach the sources
questions.explanation: Several VAs on separate hosts or sites keep tasks running when one fails. Different passphrases would break decryption across the cluster.

questions.stem: Match each data path or store to how it is protected.

pairs.match: Outbound TLS started by the VA
Encrypted with the VA cluster's key
Encryption at rest such as AES-256
LDAPS when SSL is enabled on the source

targets_extra: Plain HTTP limited by an IP allow list
questions.explanation: Each hop and store has its own control; the VA-to-target hop depends on the source's own settings.

questions.stem: Put the steps for adding a new VA to an existing cluster in order.
items: Deploy and start the VA virtual machine from the SailPoint image
Sign in as the sailpoint user and change the default password
Run va-bootstrap set-passphrase with the cluster's existing passphrase
Run va-bootstrap pair and enter the pairing code on the cluster's new VA page
Confirm the new VA shows as connected and healthy in the cluster
questions.explanation: The VM comes up first, the default password is changed, the shared passphrase is set so the VA can use the cluster's key, the VA is paired to the cluster, and its status is checked before relying on it.
